at: The night before, the Baekje king sits by a fire
scene: Low three-quarter, night on the south bank of the Taedong. King Gunchogo of Baekje (face from the sheet) sits on a camp stool by a small fire, elbows on knees, staring across black water at the dark wall of Pyongyang; the fire lights his face from below in gold. Behind him a vast night sky FULL of small golden-yellow stars, thick as spilled grain, the only colour in the frame. Far left on the riverbank, tiny and half in mist, the pale white-gold guardian stag watches him. FLASHBACK MOOD: an old memory shrouded in darkness — at least seventy percent of the frame crushed ink-black, mist and shadow swallowing the edges like a half-remembered dream, one hard key light carving the king out; more tenebristic and dramatic than the present-day stills. The sky motif is a symbolic metaphor, painted large and quiet. The guardian animal is a SMALL SUBTLE cameo, half-hidden in shadow or mist, easy to miss, copied from the attached animal board.

at: The arrow that finds him isn’t aimed at anyone

Rain of arrows as thin dark streaks. Above, the sky is black but scattered with faint golden-yellow stars, the southern king's stars, dimly over the north. On a merlon in shadow, tiny, a black three-legged crow.
